account:
Something seems to be happening around the bakery and bread deliveries, but I still cannot say exactly what. Several townspeople independently repeat a claim about a bridge or port change at the bakery. Townsfolk 11 named the baker, freight, innkeeper and neighbour as having been there, and reported the builder carrying a sack of bread at the bakery and square_north_1. Today another townsman reported the builder with a sack at the market. These are reports, not events I witnessed; repeated wording may simply mean the same rumour is circulating.

Just now I heard the baker say they could not recall exact quantities or any agreed payment, would make no payment claim without evidence, that there was no town charge, and that future orders need an agreed price. I do not know who was being addressed or what order was meant. That makes bread provisioning or some informal arrangement a plausible part of the activity, but it does not establish a bridge project, misuse of town money, or any other wrongdoing.

The innkeeper has an appointment with me in the great hall at eighteen hundred, explicitly asking me not to arrive early. Its purpose has not been explained. That is unusual and may connect to the people named in the bakery report, though it could be an innocent gathering or surprise. I intend to honour the agreed arrival time rather than presume a conspiracy.

Ordinary business has been oddly unproductive: nobody presented reserves at my scheduled mill inspection, the secretary does not know who originally arranged it, no council letters have reached the secretary, and the account ledgers remain unlocated. The treasury held 128 emeralds when I counted it yesterday; I have no evidence of missing funds. I went to the bakery before lunch but did not find the baker. I have now explicitly authorized the secretary to question the baker about the reported changes and a grain-report contact, locate the ledgers, and report at sixteen-thirty. My next appointment is tea with the neighbour at fifteen hundred, an opportunity to ask someone reportedly involved for a firsthand explanation. For now, an informal bread-related arrangement and an unexplained hall meeting are my best leads, not proven explanations.
